title: ICE to Pay LexisNexis Millions for Data to Feed to Palantir
excerpt: LexisNexis sells a massive amount of data to law enforcement, including ICE. New records indicate ICE wants to feed that data into a Palantir system.
content_html:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) plans to pay LexisNexis millions more dollars for continued access to data it can feed into a Palantir platform, according to newly published procurement records. The data is to help, among other sections, ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO), the part of ICE focused on deportation.

The documents provide some more insight into the sort of information ICE intends to use Palantir to process. In January, 404 Media revealed the existence of ELITE, a system Palantir made for ICE that helps the agency find which neighborhoods to target by bringing together data from private suppliers and government agencies.

The news comes as ICE arrested more than 51,000 people in July, many of those at airports.

💡

Do you work at LexisNexis, Palantir, or ICE? I would love to hear from you. Using a non-work device, you can message me securely on Signal at joseph.404 or send me an email at joseph@404media.co.

The data is to support “all aspects of ICE screening and vetting, lead development, and criminal analysis activities,” one of the documents says. That also includes identifying what ICE perceives as fraud “before crime and fraud can materialize and detecting and reporting elements of crimes involving the exploitation or attempts to exploit the immigration and customs laws of the United States.” ICE anticipates paying LexisNexis $6.7 million, according to the records.

LexisNexis has long provided data to ICE across multiple administrations. In this new procurement record, ICE is looking to continue access to “to LexID and Accurint Virtual Crime Center,” according to a listing posted along with the document. LexID and Accurint are LexisNexis tools that take a wealth of data — “over 82 billion public and proprietary records from more than 10,000 sources” according to the company’s website — and link them together to help law enforcement locate people.

The document suggests ICE wants to pair these capabilities and data with Palantir systems, too. One part reads, “The government's requirement is that the database must be able to application programming interface (API) with ICE applications, such as but not limited to, Palantir platform, PenLink, and ICE Data Analytics.” PenLink is another company ICE contracts with which 404 Media previously reported on. It sells social media monitoring tools and one called Webloc for tracking the location of mobile phones in entire neighborhoods.

Palantir has become a key provider of the technical infrastructure for the Trump administration’s mass deportation mission. 404 Media previously reported that the Palantir-made ELITE, or Enhanced Leads Identification & Targeting for Enforcement, populates a map interface with potential deportation targets, and provides ICE officials with a “confidence score” on the person’s current address. Sources for that tool include the Department of Health and Human Services.

It is not clear if ICE intends to ingest LexisNexis’ data into ELITE specifically or some other Palantir platform.

The document also lists several requirements around AI. They include “an artificial intelligence (AI) driven identification system” that can use data to “infer the identity of the end user,” and a facial recognition system that can leverage “large-scale image databases to perform high accuracy facial matching across diverse sources, including open-source media.” It must be able to do this in bulk, the document says.

LexisNexis, Palantir, and ICE did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

About the author

Joseph is an award-winning investigative journalist focused on generating impact. His work has triggered hundreds of millions of dollars worth of fines, shut down tech companies, and much more.

其中一份文件称，这些数据将支持“ICE 筛查和审查、先导开发和犯罪分析活动的各个方面”。 这还包括“在犯罪和欺诈发生之前识别 ICE 认为的欺诈行为，并发现和报告涉及利用或试图利用美国移民和海关法的犯罪要素。” 根据记录，ICE 预计向 LexisNexis 支付 670 万美元。

LexisNexis 长期以来一直向多个主管部门的 ICE 提供数据。 根据随文件一起发布的清单，在这份新的采购记录中，ICE 希望继续访问“LexID 和 Accurint 虚拟犯罪中心”。 LexID 和 Accurint 是 LexisNexis 的工具，它们获取大量数据——根据该公司网站，“来自 10,000 多个来源的超过 820 亿条公共和专有记录”——并将它们链接在一起，以帮助执法部门定位人员。

该文件表明 ICE 也希望将这些功能和数据与 Palantir 系统配对。 其中一部分写道：“政府的要求是数据库必须能够与 ICE 应用程序建立应用程序编程接口 (API)，例如但不限于 Palantir 平台、PenLink 和 ICE Data Analytics。” PenLink 是 404 Media 之前报道过的另一家 ICE 合同公司。 它销售社交媒体监控工具和一种名为 Webloc 的工具，用于跟踪整个社区的手机位置。

Palantir 已成为特朗普政府大规模驱逐任务的技术基础设施的主要提供商。 404 Media 此前报道称，Palantir 制造的 ELITE（即增强型线索识别和执法目标）会在地图界面中填充潜在的驱逐目标，并向 ICE 官员提供有关该人当前地址的“置信度分数”。 该工具的来源包括卫生与公众服务部。

目前尚不清楚 ICE 是否打算将 LexisNexis 的数据专门引入 ELITE 或其他 Palantir 平台。

该文件还列出了围绕人工智能的几项要求。 其中包括“人工智能（AI）驱动的识别系统”，可以使用数据“推断最终用户的身份”，以及面部识别系统，可以利用“大规模图像数据库在包括开源媒体在内的不同来源之间进行高精度面部匹配。” 文件称，它必须能够批量执行此操作。

LexisNexis、Palantir 和 ICE 没有立即回应置评请求。
